title: Higher-Round Weakness of Involutional Sboxes
summary: A two-round weakness and a derivable four-round MEDP/MELP bound are known, but whether involutional, especially naive, Sboxes cause a comparable weakness at higher rounds remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether an involutional, especially naive, Sbox causes a comparable MEDP/MELP weakness for a higher number of rounds.

scope.domain: Differential and linear cryptanalysis of involutional Sboxes, especially the naive Sbox.
parameters: Number of rounds — distinguishes the two-round behavior and four-round bound from the unresolved higher-round case
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether an involutional, especially naive, Sbox causes a comparable MEDP/MELP weakness for a higher number of rounds.

citations.label: On the Behaviors of Affine Equivalent Sboxes Regarding Differential and Linear Attacks

progress.summary: The source explicitly presents this as another open question, asking whether the two-round weakness of involutional, especially naive, Sboxes persists for more rounds. It notes that the current bound can be combined with (1) to obtain a four-round MEDP and MELP bound.
citation_labels: Anne Canteaut et al., On the Behaviors of Affine Equivalent Sboxes Regarding Differential and Linear Attacks
